Trace ordered medial-axis branches

Source: R/mat.R
trace_skeleton.Rd

Skeleton pixels with a nonpositive signed distance lie on ink and are not medial points; they are excluded before tracing on every rule, and their count is returned as attribute `skeleton_ink_excluded`. `rule="invariant"` decomposes the pixel graph (diagonal steps only where no orthogonal connection exists) into maximal paths between end/junction pixels, then prunes spurs and merges to a fixed point. A *spur* is a path from an end pixel to a junction; it is short when it has fewer than `min_points` pixels (junction included). Each round removes the shortest short spurs (all tied ones together) at every junction that keeps at least two paths afterwards; a junction where removing its tied shortest spurs would leave fewer than two paths is protected and keeps all its paths. Paths are then joined through every pixel where exactly two remain. Without ties this is sequential shortest-first spur pruning; with ties (the four equal arms of a square) every tied spur is kept, so the result does not depend on traversal order, start pixel or lattice orientation. Only spurs are pruned: a path between two junctions, or a component that is a single path, is kept whatever its length, so no skeleton component loses its last path. A closed path whose start pixel joins no other path is an isolated loop. Junction pixels are shared by the paths that meet there but never repeated within a path. `rule="mlv2023"` is the published MLV tracing: Kovesi `edgelink` with `cleanedgelist(minlength=min_points)` (Euclidean length), ported line by line, including its raster-scan traversal direction and the duplicated point at every merged junction.

Usage

trace_skeleton(mat, min_points = 10L, rule = NULL)

Arguments

mat

An mlv_mat object.

min_points

Minimum spur size: pixels for `"invariant"` (spurs only), Euclidean length for `"mlv2023"` (cleanedgelist spurs and isolated edges).

rule

Branch rule; defaults to the rule recorded in `mat`.

Value

A list of branch data frames with row, column, x, y, radius and AOF.
